formulas.formula: Your first real paycheck, your loans and your goals, all in one place. Congrats, grad.
1. Setup: your salary, taxes, 401(k) and match. It estimates your monthly take-home (or type the real one).
2. Budget: plan each category for one month. The 50/30/20 check shows Needs, Wants and Savings vs. your take-home.
3. Transactions: log paychecks and spending. Pick a category from the list.
4. Student Loans: your balances, rates and payments. See your debt-free date and what extra payments save.
5. Goals: emergency fund, moving, a car. See how much to save each month.
6. First-Year Checklist: tick off the big money moves for your first year out of school.
7. Dashboard and Monthly: how your month and year are going.
A simple guide: about 50% of take-home on Needs, 30% on Wants, 20% on Savings & debt.
If your job matches, put in at least enough to get the full match. It's an instant raise.
Start with $1,000, then build to 3 to 6 months of Needs.
Paying a little extra on your highest-rate loan saves the most interest.
Clear the white cells on Budget, Transactions, Student Loans and Goals, then update Setup.
Tinted cells: these calculate for you.
Green: on track, done, or money left.
Red: over budget, late, or something to check.
You worked hard for that degree. Now make your money work for you.
